name: COREQ, Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research
citation: Tong A, Sainsbury P, Craig J. Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research (COREQ): a 32-item checklist for interviews and focus groups. Int J Qual Health Care 2007;19(6):349-357. The 32 items keep the checklist's numbering in its three domains (research team and reflexivity 1-8, study design 9-23, analysis and findings 24-32); each topic starts with the domain's sub-heading. See https://www.equator-network.org/reporting-guidelines/coreq/

items.question: Does the report say which author or authors conducted the interviews or focus groups?
Are the researchers' credentials or qualifications given?
Is each researcher's occupation at the time of the study stated?
Is the gender of the researchers who collected the data reported?
Is the researchers' experience or training in qualitative research described?
Does the report say whether a relationship with participants existed before the study began?
Is it stated what participants were told about the researcher and the reasons for the research?
Are characteristics of the interviewer that could bear on the data (assumptions, interests, possible bias) reported?
Is the methodological orientation behind the study (for example grounded theory, ethnography, content analysis) stated?
Is the way participants were selected (for example purposive, convenience, snowball) described?
Is it stated how participants were approached (face to face, telephone, mail, email)?
Is the number of participants given?
Are the number of people who declined or dropped out, and their reasons, reported?
Is the place where data were collected (home, clinic, workplace, online) described?
Does the report say whether anyone besides the participants and researchers was present?
Are the important characteristics of the sample, such as demographics, and the collection dates given?
Were the questions or topic guide provided, and is it said whether they were pilot tested?
Does the report say whether repeat interviews were held, and how many?

items.topic: Data collection: audio or visual recording
items.question: Is it stated whether audio or visual recording was used to collect the data?
Does the report say whether field notes were taken during or after the interviews or groups?
Is the duration of the interviews or focus groups reported?
Is data saturation, or another criterion for stopping data collection, discussed?
Does the report say whether transcripts went back to participants for comment or correction?
Is the number of people who coded the data stated?
Is the coding tree, or the structure of the codes, described?
Is it said whether themes were set in advance or derived from the data?
Is any software used to manage the data named?
Does the report say whether participants gave feedback on the findings?
Are participant quotations used to illustrate the themes, each identified (for example by participant code)?
Are the data presented consistent with the findings drawn from them?
Are the major themes presented clearly in the findings?
Are diverse cases and minor themes described, not only the major ones?
